⚖️ MYTH vs FACT

❌ Myth: Every Slip Disc Requires Surgery

✅ Fact: Most patients improve without surgery.

A slip disc diagnosis can be worrying, but surgery is not the answer for everyone. In fact, most patients recover successfully with medications, physiotherapy, lifestyle modifications, and guided rehabilitation.

Surgery is generally reserved for selected situations such as persistent severe pain, progressive neurological weakness, or loss of bladder and bowel control.

The most important principle in spine care is to treat the patient's symptoms and clinical condition—not just the MRI report.

If you are experiencing back pain, leg pain, or have concerns about your MRI findings, a proper clinical evaluation can help determine the best treatment approach.

🦴 *SPINE TIP OF THE WEEK*

*THE 10-SECOND SCOLIOSIS CHECK*
*Could Your Child Have a Curved Spine?*

Many children with scoliosis have *no pain at all*, which is why it often goes unnoticed until the curve becomes more obvious.

The good news? A simple 10-second check at home can help identify early warning signs.

👀 *What to look for:*
✅ One shoulder higher than the other
✅ Uneven waistline
✅ One side of the rib cage appearing more prominent
✅ Leaning to one side while standing
✅ Uneven posture in photographs

💡 *Try this simple test:*
Ask your child to stand with feet together, bend forward, and touch their toes while you observe from behind.

Early detection can make a significant difference, especially during growth spurts between *10–16 years of age*.

Remember:
👉 Not every uneven shoulder means scoliosis.
👉 But if you notice any of these signs, it's worth getting the spine evaluated.

A quick 10-second check today could make a lifelong difference tomorrow.

📤 Please share this with parents, teachers, coaches, school groups, and anyone involved in children's health and development. Early awareness matters. 😊

🏃‍♂️ Spine Tip of the Week | The Runner's Paradox

Many runners have excellent cardiovascular fitness and endurance, but running alone may not fully protect against age-related muscle loss (sarcopenia), reduced strength, or declining bone health.

While running trains your heart, strength training helps protect your muscles, bones, joints, and spine.

Benefits of regular strength training for runners:
✅ Improved running efficiency
✅ Better spine support
✅ Reduced injury risk
✅ Stronger muscles and bones
✅ Prevention of age-related muscle loss

A simple goal: For every 3–4 running sessions per week, include at least 2 strength-training sessions. Even 20 minutes twice weekly can make a meaningful difference.

At Bombay Spine Clinic, we encourage runners and active individuals to focus on both endurance and strength for long-term spine health and injury prevention.

🦴 Spine Tip of the Week | Text Neck Syndrome

Do you spend several hours daily looking at your phone, laptop, or tablet?

Prolonged screen use can place excessive stress on the cervical spine, leading to a condition commonly known as **Text Neck Syndrome**. As the head tilts forward, the load on the neck muscles and cervical discs increases significantly, contributing to neck pain, shoulder stiffness, headaches, poor posture, and upper back discomfort.

A simple habit can help:
✅ Hold your phone closer to eye level
✅ Avoid prolonged neck flexion
✅ Take movement breaks every 20–30 minutes
✅ Perform gentle neck and upper back stretches regularly

At Bombay Spine Clinic, we frequently see patients with posture-related neck pain, cervical spondylosis, office-related neck strain, and screen-time-associated spine problems.

Early attention to posture and ergonomics can help reduce long-term stress on the spine and improve overall neck health.

Did you know tight hips and pelvic imbalance can contribute to lower back pain, poor posture, stiffness, and reduced spinal mobility?

Limited hip mobility forces the lower back to compensate, increasing stress on the lumbar spine over time. Simple hip mobility exercises and pelvic tilt movements can help improve posture, reduce back strain, and support a healthier spine.

Prolonged screen time and desk work can contribute to neck pain, upper back stiffness, eye strain, poor posture, and “tech neck syndrome.”

A simple evidence-based habit that helps:
✅ Every 20 minutes
✅ Look 20 feet away
✅ For 20 seconds

The 20-20-20 rule helps relax neck muscles, reduce screen fatigue, improve posture, and decrease strain on the cervical spine. Simple neck stretches during work breaks can further support spinal health and mobility.

Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy (DCM) is often missed in routine OPD practice and treated as simple cervical spondylosis.

Early clues include:
✔️ Hand clumsiness
✔️ Gait imbalance or frequent falls
✔️ Hoffmann’s positive sign
✔️ Progressive weakness or stiffness
✔️ Bilateral upper limb symptoms

🚨 Red Flags Requiring Urgent Referral:
* Bowel/bladder dysfunction
* Rapidly progressive weakness
* Severe gait instability
